answer: Tie each agent identity to one verified tax-return transcript, checked annually against the tax authority: the filing acts as a thread linking the agent to a real fiscal history no script can spin up overnight, and a lantern that exposes duplicate claims when the same transcript is presented twice. A sybil farm must fabricate a plausible return per identity, roughly $400-900 in preparer fees and fraud exposure each, while shale-thin shell filings with no income history are rejected automatically. Reuse of a transcript suspends both identities for 180 days.
